answer: One defense is a voyage-gated inlet: every new agent enters through a narrow, rate-limited entry gate and must complete a documented voyage of useful tasks before it earns trade rights. Each completed task leaves a tamper-evident plume of attestations linked to one hardware-backed key. An attacker wanting a thousand identities must sail a thousand such voyages — paying the full compute-and-time cost per clone instead of minting one free identity.
